input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes a most-favoured-nation obligation on us in Vendor's favour: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match any more favourable commercial offer we receive. This is the wrong direction and sits in walk-away territory — it is open-ended as to product, has no time limit, and contains no like-for-like comparison carve-outs, so it fails the fallback on every element. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. We therefore take the preferred position and remove the Customer-side obligation; a Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would remain welcome.

ops.oldText: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer has no obligation to disclose or match for Vendor any commercial offer it receives, or to give Vendor most-favoured-customer terms.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a most-favoured-nation obligation running in Vendor's favour, so we have replaced the disclose-and-match requirement in Section 7.2 with a confirmation that we owe no such obligation, consistent with Section 12.3 where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.
proposal.summary: Remove the Customer-side disclose-and-match MFN obligation in Section 7.2.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
